short_answer: Not for photos. CloudConvert is a general purpose conversion service that charges by the job, and for the everyday case, a folder of iPhone HEIC photos that need to become JPGs small enough to email or upload, a modern browser can do the whole thing itself. The free tool here converts, resizes and strips location data without sending a single byte anywhere.
paywall:
CloudConvert's free plan is a daily allowance of credits, ten a day at the time of writing, with a file size cap, and each conversion uses at least one credit and more for anything slow. Beyond that you buy credit packages or a monthly subscription priced by volume. Convertio, Zamzar and the rest of the category work the same way: a small free quota, a size limit, then a subscription.

The part the pricing pages do not dwell on is that every one of these services works by uploading your files to their servers. For a spreadsheet that is fine. For a few hundred personal photos, each carrying the GPS position of where it was taken, it is a strange trade for a job your own computer finishes in seconds.
free_does:
• Decodes HEIC and HEIF in the browser, so iPhone photos open on Windows, Android and Linux where nothing else will read them.
  • Saves as JPG, PNG or WebP at a quality you choose, resizes a whole batch to fit within a chosen size, and can keep every file under a size limit for email or marketplace uploads.
  • Removes EXIF metadata on the way out: GPS position, device, timestamps, embedded thumbnails. Marks which originals carried location data.
  • Downloads one at a time or as a single ZIP. No account, no daily quota, no file size cap beyond your browser's memory.
when_pay:
• You need formats a browser cannot produce: PDF to Word, video transcodes, vector or archive formats. That breadth is CloudConvert's actual product.
  • You want an API that converts files automatically inside your own software.
  • You are on a phone or a locked down work machine and a server doing the heavy lifting is the point.
